name: LTC1044CN8#PBF
title: LTC1044: CMOS switched-capacitor voltage converter, 1.5 V to 9 V, 7660 pin-compatible
summary: A monolithic CMOS charge pump that, with two external capacitors, inverts its supply (VOUT = -VIN); rewired it doubles, halves or, stacked, multiplies a voltage. It drops into 7660 sockets and adds a BOOST pin that raises the internal oscillator about seven times, works from 1.5 V to 9 V over the whole temperature range with no protection diode, and draws 60 µA typical (200 µA max) unloaded at 5 V. Output resistance is about 100 Ω max at 20 mA, open-circuit conversion efficiency 97 % min, power efficiency 95 % min. It comes in an 8-lead PDIP, an 8-lead TO-5 metal can and an obsolete 8-lead CERDIP.
key_figures: 60µA typ, 200µA max at V+ = 5V, RL = ∞; 20µA typ at V+ = 3V
LTC1044C -40°C to 85°C, LTC1044M -55°C to 125°C; LTC1044CN8 0°C to 70°C

notes: Grades: C is commercial, M military temperature range. Wider operating temperature ranges are available from the factory.
Some packages also come on 500-piece reels with the suffix #TRMPBF.

pins.package: N8 (8-lead PDIP), J8 (8-lead CERDIP), H (8-lead TO-5 metal can)

pins.name: BOOST
pins.function: Oscillator boost. Tied to V+ it raises the charge and discharge currents of the oscillator and so its frequency, by about seven times; left open the oscillator runs at its normal rate. Leave it open when OSC is driven from outside.

pins.name: CAP+
pins.function: Positive end of the pump capacitor C1; a polarised C1 has its + lead on this pin.

pins.name: GROUND
pins.function: Ground of the converter. In an inverter it is the circuit ground; in other circuits it is the output common (splitter) or the halved output (divider).

pins.name: CAP-
pins.function: Negative end of the pump capacitor C1.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Converter output; in the inverter it carries -V+ and the reservoir capacitor C2.

pins.name: LV
pins.function: Low-voltage pin: the bottom rail of the internal logic. Tie it to GROUND below V+ = 3V; at 3V and above an internal switch joins it to GROUND, so it may be tied to GROUND or left open.

pins.name: OSC
pins.function: Oscillator timing node (about 14pF inside). Capacitance added to ground lowers the frequency; an external clock driven into this pin sets the switching rate.

pins.name: V+
pins.function: Positive supply, 1.5V to 9V. On the H package the case is V+.

notes: The three packages share one pinout.

tables.title: Absolute maximum ratings
notes: Note 1: Going past these ratings can destroy the part, and time spent at any of them can shorten its life and reliability.
Note 2: Any input taken above V+ or below ground risks a latch-up that destroys the part. Signals from other supplies should not reach the inputs before the LTC1044 is powered.

circuits.title: Generating CMOS Logic Supply from Two Mercury Batteries
circuits.description: Two 1.2 V cells in series feed V+ and GROUND; the converter puts an inverted copy of the cell voltage below GROUND on VOUT, and that node is the logic ground. The CMOS logic sits across V+ and VOUT, so it sees about twice the cell voltage, 4.8 V. LV is joined to GROUND, as required below 3 V. The converter itself draws about 3 µA.
notes: Supply current IS ≈ 3µA.

circuits.title: Test circuit (Figure 1)
circuits.description: The part is measured as an inverter from 5 V. C1 is the pump capacitor between CAP+ and CAP-, C2 the reservoir on VOUT with its + end at ground, and RL the load, wired from V+ to VOUT so the supply current IS includes the load current IL. GROUND and LV go to ground. OSC either carries an optional capacitor COSC to ground or is switched to an external oscillator. BOOST is open.

circuits.title: External Clocking
circuits.description: An inverter whose oscillator is overdriven by a logic gate. The gate runs from V+ and ground and its output drives OSC directly; BOOST is left open. The 100 kΩ pull-up from OSC to V+ is only needed when the gate is TTL. The output is -(V+).

parts.note: needed only with a TTL gate

circuits.title: Negative Voltage Converter
circuits.description: The basic inverter: a positive supply of 1.5 V to 9 V on V+ gives VOUT = -V+ on pin 5, across the full temperature range and with no external diode. One 10 µF capacitor pumps between CAP+ and CAP-, the other holds the output. The output behaves as a near-ideal source behind about 80 Ω. The LV link to ground is needed only below 3 V.
notes: LV to ground: required for V+ < 3V.
TMIN ≤ TA ≤ TMAX.

circuits.title: Voltage Doubler (a)
circuits.description: Doubling by moving the capacitors: VIN reaches V+ through a 1N914 and reaches GROUND through R1, while VOUT is grounded. The chip then pumps V+ up to about 2VIN (3 V to 18 V), held on C2. R1 keeps GROUND from latching up above V+ at turn-on; 200 Ω is usually enough and a larger value may be needed. The 1 MΩ from LV to ground lets the oscillator start when VIN is under 3 V.

circuits.title: Voltage Doubler (b)
circuits.description: A diode doubler driven from CAP+: VIN on V+ feeds the anode of the first diode; its cathode meets the + end of the first 10 µF capacitor and the anode of the second diode, whose cathode carries the output and the second 10 µF capacitor. The - end of the first capacitor is on CAP+. VOUT = 2(VIN - 1) for VIN from 1.5 V to 9 V. GROUND is at ground; LV is grounded below 3 V; CAP-, VOUT, BOOST and OSC are unused.
notes: LV to ground: required for V+ < 3V.

circuits.title: Ultra Precision Voltage Divider
circuits.description: V+ (3 V to 18 V) goes in at pin 8 and pin 5 is grounded; the switched capacitor settles GROUND (pin 3) at half the input, V+/2 to within ±0.002 % over temperature when the load is kept to 100 nA or less. LV is joined to the midpoint when V+ is under 6 V.
notes: LV to the V+/2 node: required for V+ < 6V.
TMIN ≤ TA ≤ TMAX, IL ≤ 100nA.

circuits.title: Battery Splitter
circuits.description: A 9 V battery across V+ and VOUT is split into +VB/2 and -VB/2 (+4.5 V and -4.5 V) about pin 3, which becomes the output common. C2 holds the lower half. LV joins the common when VB is under 6 V. VB may be 3 V to 18 V.
notes: LV to output common: required for VB < 6V.
3V ≤ VB ≤ 18V.

circuits.title: Paralleling for Lower Output Resistance
circuits.description: Two inverters share V+, ground and one 20 µF output capacitor, so their output resistances sit in parallel. One gate of a CD4077 (exclusive-NOR) compares the CAP+ nodes of the two converters and drives the second one's OSC pin, keeping the two in step so the ripple stays low. VOUT = -(V+).

circuits.title: Stacking for Higher Voltage
circuits.description: Two converters in a stack. The first inverts V+ to -(V+), and that node is the GROUND of the second. The second's V+ pin goes, selected by a switch, either to ground, which gives VOUT = -2V+, or to V+, which gives VOUT = -3V+. The output current available falls with the product of the two efficiencies and with the step-up ratio.

parts.value: U2 V+ to V+ (VOUT = -3V+) or to ground (VOUT = -2V+)

circuits.title: Voltage Tripler/Quadrupler
circuits.description: Two doublers of the R-and-diode kind in a stack. The first lifts +5 V to 2V+ (+10 V). The second takes +10 V on its V+ (through a 1N914) and its GROUND (through 200 Ω); its VOUT pin goes, selected by a switch, either to the first chip's GROUND pin, about V+, for VOUT = 3V+ (+15 V), or to ground for VOUT = 4V+ (+20 V). The 1 MΩ resistors from LV to ground are needed only when V+ is under 3 V.

parts.value: U2 VOUT to U1 GROUND (VOUT = 3V+) or to ground (VOUT = 4V+)

circuits.title: Low Output Impedance Voltage Converter
circuits.description: An LM10 op amp and reference drive the V+ pin of an inverter, closing a loop around its negative output. The LM10 output feeds V+ of the converter (with 100 µF to ground); the converter output is the OUTPUT node, and 200 kΩ from it back to the LM10's + input closes the loop. The 8.2 kΩ and the 50 kΩ VOUT ADJ set the output level; a 39 kΩ from the LM10 - input to its reference pin, a 39 kΩ to ground and 0.1 µF to the LM10 output complete the network. Load regulation is ±0.02 % from 0 mA to 15 mA, with VIN at least |-VOUT| + 0.5 V.

parts.note: op amp and reference; pins by number

notes: VIN ≥ |-VOUT| + 0.5V.
Load regulation ±0.02%, 0mA to 15mA.

circuits.title: Single 5V Strain Gauge Bridge Signal Conditioner
circuits.description: A pressure-bridge amplifier run from 5 V alone. The converter makes -5 V for the LT1013's negative supply. An LT1004 fed by 220 Ω from 5 V gives 1.2 V, which excites the top of the 350 Ω bridge and is also brought out (1 mA at most) as the reference for an A/D converter so readings are ratiometric. One LT1013 half drives the bottom of the bridge to about -1.2 V so the bridge's other corner (E) holds 0 V. The other half amplifies the signal at corner A, after a 100 kΩ and 0.33 µF filter, with gain set by 46 kΩ plus the 2 kΩ trim over 100 Ω; the 10 kΩ zero trim feeds offset in through 301 kΩ. The output is 0 V to 3.5 V for 0 psi to 350 psi.

parts.note: potentiometer, ZERO TRIM; ends 1 and 2, wiper W
350Ω pressure transducer bridge; pins A, C, D, E
dual op amp; pins by number

notes: Transducer pins A, C, D, E are its lettered terminals.

circuits.title: Regulated Output 3V to 5V Converter
circuits.description: A 3 V battery (Eveready EXP-30) is doubled and regulated to 5 V. The converter is wired as an R-and-diode doubler: 200 Ω from 3 V to GROUND, a 1N914 from 3 V to V+, VOUT to the battery return, and the 5 V output on V+ with 100 µF. Two PNP transistors in parallel, emitters on CAP- and collectors on the pump capacitor's negative end, and an LM10 drives their bases through 1 kΩ each. The LM10 compares the output, divided by 4.8 MΩ against 150 kΩ plus a 100 kΩ trim, with its reference. A 330 kΩ and a 1N914 bias the op amp's + input; 1 MΩ ties LV to the return.

parts.note: op amp and reference; pins by number

circuits.title: Low Dropout 5V Regulator
circuits.description: A 5 V linear regulator from four 1.5 V cells (6 V) with a 2N2219 pass transistor and very low dropout. The converter, as an R-and-diode doubler from the battery, makes about +12 V to supply the LT1013. The feedback half compares the output, divided by 120 kΩ against 30 kΩ plus a 50 kΩ OUTPUT ADJUST, with the LT1004's 1.2 V and drives the base through 100 Ω. The other half watches the 0.01 Ω in the battery return against a fraction of the reference (1 MΩ over 1.2 kΩ) and, through a 1N914, pulls the feedback node up to limit short-circuit current. Dropout is 1 mV at 1 mA, 15 mV at 10 mA and 95 mV at 100 mA.

parts.note: dual op amp; pins by number

notes: VDROPOUT at 1mA = 1mV, at 10mA = 15mV, at 100mA = 95mV.

operation.text: A capacitor C1 is switched back and forth between a source V1 and an output V2 that is held by C2. Each cycle it takes charge C1 × V1 and gives up enough to fall to V2, so the charge moved per cycle is C1(V1 - V2) and f cycles a second make a current. The capacitor therefore looks like a resistor of 1/(f × C1). Inside the LTC1044 an oscillator and a divide-by-two make two opposite phases: in one, switches join CAP+ to V+ and CAP- to GROUND; in the other they join CAP+ to GROUND and CAP- to VOUT, so C1 is charged from the supply and then emptied into C2 upside down. Finite switch on-resistance and output ripple make the simple model inexact.

In the inverter the output looks like a near-ideal source behind about 80Ω. Two terms make that up: the switched-capacitor resistance 1/((fOSC/2) × C1) and the on-resistance of the MOS switches. With C1 = C2 = 10µF the output resistance rises from 60Ω at fOSC = 10kHz to 200Ω at 1kHz; once 1/fC is large against the switch resistance it alone sets the output resistance. Losses, and so efficiency, follow the output resistance: at low frequency the 1/fC1 term takes over and efficiency falls. At high frequency efficiency falls again, because a little charge is lost every switching cycle and that loss times the frequency is a current.

The internal logic is supplied between V+ and LV. When V+ is 3V or more an internal switch connects LV to GROUND, so LV may be tied to GROUND or left open. Below 3V LV must be tied to GROUND. The absolute maximum current into pin 6 is 20µA.

The oscillator charges and discharges about 14pF on OSC between current sources, with a Schmitt trigger switching the direction. Tying BOOST to V+ switches in sources six times larger, raising the frequency about seven times; a higher frequency lowers the output resistance and the ripple at heavier loads. Capacitance added from OSC to ground lowers the frequency, and BOOST together with an OSC capacitor covers a wide range of frequencies. To clock the part from outside, drive OSC and leave BOOST open. OSC sources or sinks only about 0.5µA, so a logic gate can drive it. A CMOS gate suits it best, as it works from 3V to 15V and swings far enough for the Schmitt trigger; in a 5V system a TTL gate works with a pull-up resistor (100k) from OSC to V+.

Earlier converters of this type needed a diode between VOUT and the reservoir capacitor C2 above 6.5V (5V over the military temperature range). The LTC1044 works from 1.5V to 9V across all temperature ranges without it. Existing 7660 designs that include the diode still work, provided V+ stays at or below 9V.

C1 and C2 are not critical: they need not match, need not be precise and need not be of high quality. Aluminium or tantalum electrolytics serve well; only cost and size decide. At low frequency the pump capacitor sets most of the output resistance.
Any input taken above V+ or below ground can latch the part up destructively. Inputs fed from other supplies should not be live before the LTC1044 is powered.

Rearranging the two capacitors makes a doubler (circuit doubler-a): VIN goes to V+ through a diode and to GROUND through R1, VOUT is grounded, and V+ rises to 2VIN. Below 3V input a 1MΩ resistor from LV to ground is needed for the oscillator to start. During turn-on GROUND is pulled above V+, which can latch the part; the latch-up does no damage but stops the doubling, and R1 prevents it. 200Ω is enough in most cases; a larger value may be needed to make start-up certain. R1 drops 2 × IOUT × R1; when that is more than two diode drops (1.4V silicon, 0.8V Schottky) circuit doubler-a is the recommended choice, and that circuit has no start-up problem. The second doubler (doubler-b) uses CAP+ to pump two diodes and gives 2(VIN - 1).

With the input across V+ and VOUT, GROUND sits at half the input. Accuracy of ±0.002% (±20ppm) needs a load current under 100nA; the load can be heavier at some cost in accuracy. The 0.0002% figure in the text is a misprint for 0.002%.

A single battery across V+ and VOUT yields equal positive and negative outputs of half the battery voltage, both referred to pin 3, which serves as output common. It suits small load currents. When the voltage from pin 8 to pin 5 is under 6V, LV is joined to pin 3 as well.

Two converters in parallel give a lower output resistance. When the output resistance is mostly 1/fC1, a larger C1 or a higher frequency helps more than paralleling. Two converters stacked give a negative doubler or tripler, or a positive tripler or quadrupler; in each the available output current is cut by the product of the stages' power efficiencies and by the step-up ratio.
